audience.summary: People commissioning or buying a garment who care how it is cut, finished and worn — often for a wedding, a naming ceremony, a promotion or a considered purchase for themselves.

assertions.text: The primary audience is the person making this decision in Accra: someone comparing two or three local options on a phone and looking for evidence that this business can do the job.
Local context matters: fitting appointments, the studio address, fabric lead times and the deposit around Accra should be answered before a visitor is asked to enquire.

positioning.summary: The approved Brand Kit describes this business as quietly confident, exacting, warm, crafted. Editorial and unhurried: a warm paper ground, one deep kente red used like a stamp, cloth photographed close and type given room to speak.

assertions.text: Personality: quietly confident, exacting, warm, crafted.
Tone of voice: Plain, precise and proud of the craft. Short sentences; name the cloth, the cut and the fitting.
Positioning is a design argument, not a claim about the market: the direction should make the business recognisable without inventing an award, a client list or a heritage.

objectives.summary: Book a fitting or start a commission through WhatsApp, with the price range and lead time answered before the first message. The site has one primary conversion; everything else supports it.

assertions.text: Primary conversion supported by the current site: message on WhatsApp.

evidence.note: Inferred from the contact or selling route the page publishes.

assertions.text: Measure the direction by qualified enquiries, not by time on page: a completed message on WhatsApp with the information the business needs to reply.
The primary action appears in the first viewport on mobile and again at the end of the story; no competing secondary action may look equally important.

atmosphere.summary: Intimate, exacting and unhurried. The work should feel handled rather than marketed: cloth, hands, fitting, finish. The atmosphere is a creative proposal, not a description of how the business already feels; it should be tested in review and refined, not asserted in copy.

assertions.text: Proposed emotional register: quietly confident, exacting, warm. Every section should hold that register; a playful illustration or a neon gradient would break it.

Avoid the default local-business mood: stock handshakes, generic “Welcome to Nsroma Atelier”, gold gradients and template testimonials. If the business has no testimonial yet, leave the space empty and say so.

storytelling.summary: The page should read as a sequence, not a list of sections: A commission begins with a conversation → Cloth, measurement and the first cut → The fitting and the finish → A piece that is worn, not archived. Each chapter earns the next; no chapter is a grid of unsupported claims.

assertions.text: Proposed narrative arc: A commission begins with a conversation; Cloth, measurement and the first cut; The fitting and the finish; A piece that is worn, not archived.
Photography and copy must come from the business. A narrative built on stock images of another place is not this business’s story and will be rejected in review.

artDirection.summary: Editorial and unhurried: a warm paper ground, one deep kente red used like a stamp, cloth photographed close and type given room to speak. The direction below extends that approved visual direction rather than replacing it.

assertions.text: Approved visual direction: Editorial and unhurried: a warm paper ground, one deep kente red used like a stamp, cloth photographed close and type given room to speak.
Materials and texture: cloth, thread, paper patterns, brass fittings. One material may be exaggerated; all of them may not.
External references are recorded as links and notes only, with a licence status. Nothing is downloaded, traced, recoloured or presented as the Studio’s own.

layout.summary: The direction will compare at least three different composition families — not one layout with three colourways. Each must state its grid, navigation, hero idea and how it collapses at 360px.

assertions.text: Composition is chosen for the business, not for the component library: editorial columns, a cinematic frame, an asymmetric offset, a catalogue index, a quiet centre and a modular block system are all available.
Avoid the default card wall: equal rounded panels with shadows and icons are not a design idea. If a card is used, it must have a reason and a different span.
Every composition is drawn mobile-first at 360px and checked at 768px and 1440px; no essential content may appear only on a wide screen.

typography.summary: Fraunces for display and Inter for text. The transitional serif display face carries the voice while the grotesque sans body face keeps reading effortless. Soft, high-contrast serifs with a small x-height at light weights; keep display sizes large, avoid long body copy below 18px, and use the optical-size axis rather than a synthetic scale.

assertions.text: Approved Brand Kit type: Display — Fraunces (300–700), SIL Open Font License 1.1.
Licences: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Both permit web embedding and self-hosting. The Studio does not download or redistribute font files without permission.
Language coverage is confirmed for English. If the site will publish Twi, Ewe, Ga or Dagbani, the pairing must change to a family with documented orthography coverage.

colour.summary: Colour is a system with roles, not a collection of swatches: a ground, a surface, ink, secondary ink, one accent and the text that sits on it. Contrast is computed before the palette is proposed.

assertions.text: Approved Brand Kit palette (version 1): Warm paper #F4EDE3, Ink #241E1A, Kente red #7A1F3D, Brass #B98A44.
Contrast checks: 14.17:1, 13.34:1, 4.59:1, 9.47:1, 3.06:1. Text pairs are adjusted until they meet WCAG 2.2 AA; a palette that fails contrast is not a direction.
The accent is used sparingly and for one job: action, emphasis or a single material note. Multiple accents, decorative gradients and coloured cards are rejected in review.

photography.summary: Work from 2 approved files in the vault, art-directed for cloth, fit and hands.

assertions.text: kente-gown-fitting.jpg (Client-owned photography) — product photo, approved for private prototype use.
seam-detail.jpg (Client-owned photography) — product photo, approved for private prototype use.
Approved mark: nsroma-mark.png (Client-supplied mark). The mark may appear in the prototype; it does not license the site for publication.
Remote images are references, never assets: they are not fetched, cached, displayed inline or offered as “use this image”. A new upload with provenance is the only route into the vault.

motion.summary: One motion idea carries the page: a reveal, a transition or a mask — never all of them at once. Motion clarifies sequence, gives feedback and then gets out of the way.

assertions.text: Every movement has a reduced-motion alternative that removes translation and scroll-linking while leaving the content visible and the focus order intact.
Only opacity, transform and clip-path may be animated; durations stay under 900ms and no motion may delay the first readable frame.
Hover is never the only route to information, and the primary action is never hidden behind an animation.

mobile.summary: The phone is the first canvas, not a compressed desktop. Composition, type and imagery are drawn at 360px before they are expanded.

assertions.text: Body text stays at or above 16px, tap targets at or above 44px, and no horizontal scrolling is permitted at 360px.
The primary action (message on WhatsApp) is reachable in the first viewport and repeated at the end; navigation uses the same labels and order at every width.
Images are cropped for portrait first, with explicit dimensions to prevent layout shift; no full-bleed video is required to understand the page.

accessibility.summary: Accessibility is a constraint on the art direction, not a clean-up task after it. A concept that cannot meet WCAG 2.2 AA is not finished.

assertions.text: WCAG 2.2 AA: text contrast at least 4.5:1, large text and UI at least 3:1, visible focus, logical heading order and labels for every control.
Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion; no content flashes more than three times per second; animation can be paused or is not essential.
The business must supply or approve alt text, captions and transcripts for its own photography, video and audio before publication.

concepts.name: The Cutting Archive
concepts.idea: Present the business as a body of work that has been documented with care, where every object carries its date, material and maker. For Nsroma Atelier in Accra, that means the work is about cloth, cut, fitting and the finish of a garment.
concepts.narrative: The page behaves like an archive opened on a table: a strong left column of writing, marginal notes, and photographs that interrupt the text rather than illustrate it. Nothing is hurried; the visitor is trusted to read. The opening line, “Begin with the material.”, is a creative proposal and will be replaced or approved with the business’s own wording before publication.

typography.rationale: Fraunces for display and Inter for text. The transitional serif display face carries the voice while the grotesque sans body face keeps reading effortless. Soft, high-contrast serifs with a small x-height at light weights; keep display sizes large, avoid long body copy below 18px, and use the optical-size axis rather than a synthetic scale. The direction keeps the approved Brand Kit face and changes the supporting voice and scale.

concepts.name: The Pattern Index
concepts.idea: Treat the whole business as a precise catalogue: numbered entries, tabular facts, and a typographic system that behaves like a well-set index. For Nsroma Atelier in Accra, that means the work is about cloth, cut, fitting and the finish of a garment.
concepts.narrative: The homepage starts with a definition and the first three entries, not a hero image. Each entry carries its material, price band and availability in a fixed metadata column. The visitor can see the range immediately and trust that the list is complete. The opening line, “Everything we make, in order.”, is a creative proposal and will be replaced or approved with the business’s own wording before publication.

Soft, high-contrast serifs with a small x-height at light weights; keep display sizes large, avoid long body copy below 18px, and use the optical-size axis rather than a synthetic scale. The direction keeps the approved Brand Kit face and changes the supporting voice and scale.

concepts.name: The Evening Cut
concepts.idea: Design the first ten seconds as an arrival: one place, one horizon, one line of type, and enough quiet for the visitor to want to step inside. For Nsroma Atelier in Accra, that means the work is about cloth, cut, fitting and the finish of a garment.
concepts.narrative: A full-bleed frame holds the opening. Type enters like a title card and then recedes. The page unfolds in scenes, each one a different hour of the same place, with the practical details arriving only after the atmosphere has earned attention. The opening line, “Arrive slowly.”, is a creative proposal and will be replaced or approved with the business’s own wording before publication.

typography.rationale: Fraunces for display and Work Sans for text. The transitional serif display face carries the voice while the grotesque sans body face keeps reading effortless. Soft, high-contrast serifs with a small x-height at light weights; keep display sizes large, avoid long body copy below 18px, and use the optical-size axis rather than a synthetic scale. The direction keeps the approved Brand Kit face and changes the supporting voice and scale.

colour.strategy: A dark, warm ground with bone-white type and one brass accent. The accent belongs to light and action, not to decoration. Contrast is checked against the dark ground, not assumed.

composition.label: Cinematic full bleed
composition.grid: 6 columns, 16px gutter, margins 16px mobile / 40px desktop, maximum 1600px. A shallow six-column overlay grid over full-width media; text is placed, never poured.
composition.navigation: A transparent bar over the first frame that becomes solid after the first scroll; the menu opens as a full-screen sequence, not a dropdown.
composition.hero: Full-viewport image with one short line of type, a quiet scroll cue and no buttons competing with the photograph.
composition.spacing: Scenes rather than sections: each image-led block earns a viewport, with quieter typographic interludes between.
composition.imageComposition: Full-bleed, wide crops with a consistent grade; occasional inset detail at 4:5 to slow the sequence.

imagery.direction: Three frames of the same place at different hours, plus one human detail: a hand pouring, a door left open, linen in low light. The image is the first argument.
imagery.treatment: Wide, cinematic crops with a consistent warm grade; one inset detail. Explicit width and height, art-directed mobile crop, no autoplay sound.
missing: Commission a short set at the hour guests actually arrive: one wide establishing frame, two details, one human moment.

rationale.audience: People commissioning or buying a garment who care how it is cut, finished and worn — often for a wedding, a naming ceremony, a promotion or a considered purchase for themselves. The Evening Cut answers that by hospitality is sold by the quality of an imagined arrival.
rationale.business: For Nsroma Atelier in Accra, the direction puts cloth, cut, fitting and the finish of a garment at the centre rather than treating the website as a container for services. It accepts the trade-offs below in exchange for a specific point of view.
